items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: Buddy was playing at the Celebrity Club and Nathan Larkins was upstairs and so we just all got together, reunion or sort of, and we just started jamming up there and blowing.

ctx.x: No lanyard. No, they don't know what the hell, what that is. No, no second line? No, no, no, no. You didn't read the little article about the second line. I was telling Segura yesterday that people are alike all over. And I met up with Buddy Tate up in New York, and I was on one of my visits up there. And Milton Larkins, and I said, man, let's march these cats around the place. He said, man, they don't know nothing about that up here. Yeah. I said, okay, watch me. Yeah. So I got to playing, and I dug a cat in the…
The third reel of Don Albert, September 18, 1972. We were talking about Buddy Tate, you were up there in New York. You were sitting in or something and you guys started dancing?

items.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: Did you know a singer by the name of Melvin Moore? He used to sing with Ernie Fields for a long time, and Don Albert out of San Antonio.

ctx.x: Yeah, I heard he was. Melvin Moore told me this. Did you know a singer by the name of Melvin Moore? He used to sing with Ernie Fields for a long time, and Don Albert out of San Antonio. And I think he told me that Ernie’s still going, still around, with us.
Tell us about some of your better recordings with the Basie band.
